summary: Medium Armor (5 Minutes to Don and 1 Minute to Doff): AC 14 + Dex modifier (max 2)

name: Splint Armor
summary: Heavy Armor (10 Minutes to Don and 5 Minutes to Doff): AC 17

name: Studded Leather Armor
summary: Light Armor (1 Minute to Don or Doff): AC 12 + Dex modifier

name: Ability Score Improvement
summary: Increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or increase two ability scores of your choice by 1.

name: Alert
summary: Benefits: Initiative Proficiency, Initiative Swap.

name: Archery
summary: You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with Ranged weapons.

name: Boon of Combat Prowess
summary: Benefits: Ability Score Increase, Peerless Aim.

name: Boon of Dimensional Travel
summary: Benefits: Ability Score Increase, Blink Steps.

name: Boon of Fate
summary: Benefits: Ability Score Increase, Improve Fate.

name: Boon of Irresistible Offense
summary: Benefits: Ability Score Increase, Overcome Defenses, Overwhelming Strike.

name: Boon of Spell Recall
summary: Benefits: Ability Score Increase, Free Casting.

name: Boon of the Night Spirit
summary: Benefits: Ability Score Increase, Merge with Shadows, Shadowy Form.

name: Boon of Truesight
summary: Benefits: Ability Score Increase, Truesight.

name: Defense
summary: While you’re wearing Light, Medium, or Heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

name: Grappler
summary: Benefits: Ability Score Increase, Punch and Grab, Attack Advantage, Fast Wrestler.

name: Great Weapon Fighting
summary: When you roll damage for an attack you make with a Melee weapon that you are holding with two hands, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3.

name: Magic Initiate
summary: Benefits: Two Cantrips, Level 1 Spell, Spell Change.

name: Savage Attacker
summary: You’ve trained to deal particularly damaging strikes.

name: Skilled
summary: You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools of your choice.

name: Two-Weapon Fighting
summary: When you make an extra attack as a result of using a weapon that has the Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren’t already adding it to the damage.

name: Acid
summary: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a vial of Acid.

name: Alchemist’s Fire
summary: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Alchemist’s Fire.

name: Ammunition
summary: Ammunition is required by a weapon that has the Ammunition property.

name: Antitoxin
summary: As a Bonus Action, you can drink a vial of Antitoxin to gain Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.

name: Arcane Focus
summary: An Arcane Focus takes one of the forms in the Arcane Focuses table and is bejeweled or carved to channel arcane magic.

name: Backpack
summary: A Backpack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot.

name: Ball Bearings
summary: As a Utilize action, you can spill Ball Bearings from their pouch.

name: Barrel
summary: A Barrel holds up to 40 gallons of liquid or up to 4 cubic feet of dry goods.

name: Basket
summary: A Basket holds up to 40 pounds within 2 cubic feet.

name: Bedroll
summary: A Bedroll sleeps one Small or Medium creature.

name: Bell
summary: When rung as a Utilize action, a Bell produces a sound that can be heard up to 60 feet away.

name: Blanket
summary: While wrapped in a blanket, you have Advantage on saving throws against extreme cold (see “Gameplay Toolbox”).

name: Block and Tackle
summary: A Block and Tackle allows you to hoist up to four times the weight you can normally lift.

name: Book
summary: A Book contains fiction or nonfiction.

name: Bottle, Glass
summary: A Glass Bottle holds up to 11/2 pints.

name: Bucket
summary: A Bucket holds up to half a cubic foot of contents.

name: Burglar’s Pack
summary: A Burglar’s Pack contains the following items: Backpack, Ball Bearings, Bell, 10 Candles, Crowbar, Hooded Lantern, 7 flasks of Oil, 5 days of Rations, Rope, Tinderbox, and Waterskin.

name: Caltrops
summary: As a Utilize action, you can spread Caltrops from their bag to cover a 5-foot-square area within 5 feet of yourself.

name: Candle
summary: For 1 hour, a lit Candle sheds Bright Light in a 5-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 5 feet.

name: Case, Crossbow Bolt
summary: A Crossbow Bolt Case holds up to 20 Bolts.

name: Case, Map or Scroll
summary: A Map or Scroll Case holds up to 10 sheets of paper or 5 sheets of parchment.

name: Chain
summary: As a Utilize action, you can wrap a Chain around an unwilling creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check.

name: Chest
summary: A Chest holds up to 12 cubic feet of contents.

name: Climber’s Kit
summary: A Climber’s Kit includes boot tips, gloves, pitons, and a harness.

name: Clothes, Fine
summary: Fine Clothes are made of expensive fabrics and adorned with expertly crafted details.

name: Clothes, Traveler’s
summary: Traveler’s Clothes are resilient garments designed for travel in various environments.

name: Component Pouch
summary: A Component Pouch is watertight and filled with compartments that hold all the free Material components of your spells.

name: Costume
summary: While wearing a Costume, you have Advantage on any ability check you make to impersonate the person or type of person it represents.

name: Crowbar
summary: Using a Crowbar gives you Advantage on Strength checks where the Crowbar’s leverage can be applied.

name: Diplomat’s Pack
summary: A Diplomat’s Pack contains the following items: Chest, Fine Clothes, Ink, 5 Ink Pens, Lamp, 2 Map or Scroll Cases, 4 flasks of Oil, 5 sheets of Paper, 5 sheets of Parchment, Perfume, and Tinderbox.

name: Druidic Focus
summary: A Druidic Focus takes one of the forms in the Druidic Focuses table and is carved, tied with ribbon, or painted to channel primal magic.

name: Dungeoneer’s Pack
summary: A Dungeoneer’s Pack contains the following items: Backpack, Caltrops, Crowbar, 2 flasks of Oil, 10 days of Rations, Rope, Tinderbox, 10 Torches, and Waterskin.

name: Entertainer’s Pack
summary: An Entertainer’s Pack contains the following items: Backpack, Bedroll, Bell, Bullseye Lantern, 3 Costumes, Mirror, 8 flasks of Oil, 9 days of Rations, Tinderbox, and Waterskin.

name: Explorer’s Pack
summary: An Explorer’s Pack contains the following items: Backpack, Bedroll, 2 flasks of Oil, 10 days of Rations, Rope, Tinderbox, 10 Torches, and Waterskin.

name: Flask
summary: A Flask holds up to 1 pint.

name: Grappling Hook
summary: As a Utilize action, you can throw the Grappling Hook at a railing, a ledge, or another catch within 50 feet of yourself, and the hook catches on if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.

name: Healer’s Kit
summary: A Healer’s Kit has ten uses.

name: Holy Symbol
summary: A Holy Symbol takes one of the forms in the Holy Symbol table and is bejeweled or painted to channel divine magic.

name: Holy Water
summary: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a flask of Holy Water.

name: Hunting Trap
summary: As a Utilize action, you can set a Hunting Trap, which is a sawtooth steel ring that snaps shut when a creature steps on a pressure plate in the center.

name: Ink
summary: Ink comes in a 1-ounce bottle, which provides enough ink to write about 500 pages.

name: Ink Pen
summary: Using Ink, an Ink Pen is used to write or draw.

name: Jug
summary: A Jug holds up to 1 gallon.

name: Ladder
summary: A Ladder is 10 feet tall.

name: Lamp
summary: A Lamp burns Oil as fuel to cast Bright Light in a 15-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet.

name: Lantern, Bullseye
summary: A Bullseye Lantern burns Oil as fuel to cast Bright Light in a 60-foot Cone and Dim Light for an additional 60 feet.

name: Lantern, Hooded
summary: A Hooded Lantern burns Oil as fuel to cast Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet.

name: Lock
summary: A Lock comes with a key.

name: Magnifying Glass
summary: A Magnifying Glass grants Advantage on any ability check made to appraise or inspect a highly detailed item.

name: Manacles
summary: As a Utilize action, you can use Manacles to bind an unwilling Small or Medium creature within 5 feet of yourself that has the Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained condition if you succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.

name: Map
summary: If you consult an accurate Map, you gain a +5 bonus to Wisdom (Survival) checks you make to find your way in the place represented on it.

name: Mirror
summary: A handheld steel Mirror is useful for personal cosmetics but also for peeking around corners and reflecting light as a signal.

name: Net
summary: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with throwing a Net.

name: Oil
summary: You can douse a creature, object, or space with Oil or use it as fuel, as detailed below.

name: Paper
summary: One sheet of Paper can hold about 250 handwritten words.

name: Parchment
summary: One sheet of Parchment can hold about 250 handwritten words.

name: Perfume
summary: Perfume comes in a 4-ounce vial.

name: Poison, Basic
summary: As a Bonus Action, you can use a vial of Basic Poison to coat one weapon or up to three pieces of ammunition.

name: Pole
summary: A Pole is 10 feet long.

name: Pot, Iron
summary: An Iron Pot holds up to 1 gallon.

name: Potion of Healing
summary: This potion is a magic item.

name: Pouch
summary: A Pouch holds up to 6 pounds within one-fifth of a cubic foot.

name: Priest’s Pack
summary: A Priest’s Pack contains the following items: Backpack, Blanket, Holy Water, Lamp, 7 days of Rations, Robe, and Tinderbox.

name: Quiver
summary: A Quiver holds up to 20 Arrows.

name: Ram, Portable
summary: You can use a Portable Ram to break down doors.

name: Rations
summary: Rations consist of travel-ready food, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts.

name: Robe
summary: A Robe has vocational or ceremonial significance.

name: Rope
summary: As a Utilize action, you can tie a knot with Rope if you succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.

name: Sack
summary: A Sack holds up to 30 pounds within 1 cubic foot.

name: Scholar’s Pack
summary: A Scholar’s Pack contains the following items: Backpack, Book, Ink, Ink Pen, Lamp, 10 flasks of Oil, 10 sheets of Parchment, and Tinderbox.

name: Shovel
summary: Working for 1 hour, you can use a Shovel to dig a hole that is 5 feet on each side in soil or similar material.

name: Signal Whistle
summary: When blown as a Utilize action, a Signal Whistle produces a sound that can be heard up to 600 feet away.

name: Spell Scroll
summary: A Spell Scroll (Cantrip) or Spell Scroll (Level 1) is a magic item that bears the words of a cantrip or level 1 spell, respectively, determined by the scroll’s creator.

name: Spikes, Iron
summary: Iron Spikes come in bundles of ten.

name: Spyglass
summary: Objects viewed through a Spyglass are magnified to twice their size.

name: String
summary: String is 10 feet long.

name: Tent
summary: A Tent sleeps up to two Small or Medium creatures.

name: Tinderbox
summary: A Tinderbox is a small container holding flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire.

name: Torch
summary: A Torch burns for 1 hour, casting Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet.

name: Vial
summary: A Vial holds up to 4 ounces.

name: Waterskin
summary: A Waterskin holds up to 4 pints.

name: Ability Check
summary: An ability check is a D20 Test that represents using one of the six abilities—or a specific skill associated with an ability—to overcome a challenge.

name: Ability Score and Modifier
summary: A creature has six ability scores—Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma—each of which has a corresponding modifier.

name: Action
summary: On your turn, you can take one action.

name: Advantage
summary: If you have Advantage on a D20 Test, roll two d20s, and use the higher roll.

name: Adventure
summary: An adventure is a series of encounters.

name: Alignment
summary: A creature’s alignment broadly describes its ethical attitudes and ideals.

name: Ally
summary: A creature is your ally if it is a member of your adventuring party, your friend, on your side in combat, or a creature that the rules or the GM designates as your ally.

name: Area of Effect
summary: The descriptions of many spells and other features specify that they have an area of effect, which typically has one of six shapes.

name: Armor Class
summary: An Armor Class (AC) is the target number for an attack roll.

name: Armor Training
summary: Armor training allows you to use armor of a certain category without the following drawbacks.

name: Attack
summary: When you take the Attack action, you can make one attack roll with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

name: Attack Roll
summary: An attack roll is a D20 Test that represents making an attack with a weapon, an Unarmed Strike, or a spell.

name: Attitude
summary: A monster has a starting attitude toward a player character: Friendly, Hostile, or Indifferent.

name: Attunement
summary: Some magic items require a creature to form a bond—called Attunement—with them before the creature can use an item’s magical properties.

name: Blinded
summary: While you have the Blinded condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Blindsight
summary: If you have Blindsight, you can see within a specific range without relying on physical sight.

name: Bloodied
summary: A creature is Bloodied while it has half its Hit Points or fewer remaining.

name: Bonus Action
summary: A Bonus Action is a special action that you can take on the same turn that you take an action.

name: Breaking Objects
summary: Objects can be harmed by attacks and by some spells, using the rules below.

name: Bright Light
summary: Bright Light is normal illumination.

name: Burning
summary: A burning creature or object takes 1d4 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

name: Burrow Speed
summary: A creature that has a Burrow Speed can use that speed to move through sand, earth, mud, or ice.

name: Campaign
summary: A campaign is a series of adventures.

name: Cantrip
summary: A cantrip is a level 0 spell, which is cast without a spell slot.

name: Carrying Capacity
summary: Your size and Strength score determine the maximum weight in pounds that you can carry, as shown in the Carrying Capacity table.

name: Challenge Rating
summary: Challenge Rating (CR) summarizes the threat a monster poses to a group of four player characters.

name: Character Sheet
summary: A character sheet is a paper or digital record that you use to track your character’s information.

name: Charmed
summary: While you have the Charmed condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Climb Speed
summary: A Climb Speed can be used in place of Speed to traverse a vertical surface without expending the extra movement normally associated with climbing.

name: Climbing
summary: While you’re climbing, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot (2 extra feet in Difficult Terrain).

name: Concentration
summary: Some spells and other effects require Concentration to remain active, as specified in their descriptions.

name: Condition
summary: A condition is a temporary game state.

name: Cone
summary: A Cone is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a point of origin in a direction its creator chooses.

name: Cover
summary: Cover provides a degree of protection to a target behind it.

name: Crawling
summary: While you’re crawling, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot (2 extra feet in Difficult Terrain).

name: Creature
summary: Any being in the game, including a player’s character, is a creature.

name: Creature Type
summary: Every creature, including every player character, has a tag in the rules that identifies the type of creature it is.

name: Critical Hit
summary: If you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll, you score a Critical Hit, and the attack hits regardless of any modifiers or the target’s AC.

name: Cube
summary: A Cube is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a point of origin located anywhere on a face of the Cube.

name: Curses
summary: Some game effects curse a creature or an object.

name: Cylinder
summary: A Cylinder is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a point of origin located at the center of the circular top or bottom of the Cylinder.

name: D20 Test
summary: D20 Tests encompass the three main d20 rolls of the game: ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws.

name: Damage
summary: Damage represents harm that causes a creature or an object to lose Hit Points.

name: Damage Roll
summary: A damage roll is a die roll, adjusted by any applicable modifiers, that deals damage to a target.

name: Damage Threshold
summary: A creature or an object that has a damage threshold has Immunity to all damage unless it takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, in which case it takes that entire instance of damage.

name: Damage Types
summary: Attacks and other harmful effects deal different types of damage.

name: Darkness
summary: An area of Darkness is Heavily Obscured.

name: Darkvision
summary: If you have Darkvision, you can see in Dim Light within a specified range as if it were Bright Light and in Darkness within that range as if it were Dim Light.

name: Dash
summary: When you take the Dash action, you gain extra movement for the current turn.

name: Dead
summary: A dead creature has no Hit Points and can’t regain them unless it is first revived by magic such as the Raise Dead or Revivify spell.

name: Deafened
summary: While you have the Deafened condition, you experience the following effect.

name: Death Saving Throw
summary: A player character must make a Death Saving Throw (also called a Death Save) if they start their turn with 0 Hit Points.

name: Dehydration
summary: A creature requires an amount of water per day based on its size, as shown in the Water Needs per Day table.

name: Difficult Terrain
summary: If a space is Difficult Terrain, every foot of movement in that space costs 1 extra foot.

name: Difficulty Class
summary: A Difficulty Class (DC) is the target number for an ability check or a saving throw.

name: Dim Light
summary: An area with Dim Light is Lightly Obscured.

name: Disadvantage
summary: If you have Disadvantage on a D20 Test, roll two d20s and use the lower roll.

name: Disengage
summary: If you take the Disengage action, your movement doesn’t provoke Opportunity Attacks for the rest of the current turn.

name: Dodge
summary: If you take the Dodge action, you gain the following benefits: until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against you has Disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity saving throws with Advantage.

name: Emanation
summary: An Emanation is an area of effect that extends in straight lines from a creature or an object in all directions.

name: Encounter
summary: An encounter is a scene in an adventure that is part of at least one of the game’s three pillars: social interaction, exploration, or combat.

name: Enemy
summary: A creature is your enemy if it fights against you in combat, actively works to harm you, or is designated as your enemy by the rules or GM.

name: Exhaustion
summary: While you have the Exhaustion condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Experience Points
summary: As they overcome challenges and complete adventures, characters earn Experience Points (XP), which are awarded by the Game Master.

name: Expertise
summary: Expertise is a feature that enhances your use of a skill proficiency.

name: Falling
summary: A creature that falls takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage at the end of the fall for every 10 feet it fell, to a maximum of 20d6.

name: Fly Speed
summary: A Fly Speed can be used to travel through the air.

name: Flying
summary: A variety of effects allow a creature to fly.

name: Friendly
summary: A Friendly creature views you favorably.

name: Frightened
summary: While you have the Frightened condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Grappled
summary: While you have the Grappled condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Grappling
summary: A creature can grapple another creature.

name: Hazard
summary: A hazard is an environmental danger.

name: Healing
summary: Healing is how you regain Hit Points.

name: Heavily Obscured
summary: You have the Blinded condition while trying to see something in a Heavily Obscured space.

name: Help
summary: When you take the Help action, you do one of the following.

name: Heroic Inspiration
summary: If you (a player character) have Heroic Inspiration, you can expend it to reroll any die immediately after rolling it, and you must use the new roll.

name: Hide
summary: With the Hide action, you try to hide yourself.

name: High Jump
summary: When you make a High Jump, you leap into the air a number of feet equal to 3 plus your Strength modifier (minimum of 0 feet) if you move at least 10 feet on foot immediately before the jump.

name: Hit Point Dice
summary: Hit Point Dice, or Hit Dice for short, help determine a player character’s Hit Point maximum, as explained in “Character Creation.” Most monsters also have Hit Dice.

name: Hit Points
summary: Hit Points (HP) are a measure of how difficult it is to kill or destroy a creature or an object.

name: Hostile
summary: A Hostile creature views you unfavorably.

name: Hover
summary: Some creatures can hover, as noted in their stat blocks, and some spells and other effects grant the ability to hover.

name: Illusions
summary: Spells and other effects sometimes create magical illusions.

name: Immunity
summary: If you have Immunity to a damage type or a condition, it doesn’t affect you in any way.

name: Improvised Weapons
summary: An improvised weapon is an object wielded as a makeshift weapon, such as broken glass, a table leg, or a frying pan.

name: Incapacitated
summary: While you have the Incapacitated condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Indifferent
summary: An Indifferent creature has no desire to help or hinder you.

name: Influence
summary: With the Influence action, you urge a monster to do something.

name: Initiative
summary: Initiative determines the order of turns during combat.

name: Invisible
summary: While you have the Invisible condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Jumping
summary: When you jump, you make either a Long Jump (horizontal) or a High Jump (vertical).

name: Knocking Out a Creature
summary: When you would reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with a melee attack, you can instead reduce the creature to 1 Hit Point.

name: Lightly Obscured
summary: You have Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to see something in a Lightly Obscured space.

name: Line
summary: A Line is an area of effect that extends from a point of origin in a straight path along its length and covers an area defined by its width.

name: Long Jump
summary: When you make a Long Jump, you leap horizontally a number of feet up to your Strength score if you move at least 10 feet immediately before the jump.

name: Long Rest
summary: A Long Rest is a period of extended downtime—at least 8 hours—available to any creature.

name: Magic
summary: When you take the Magic action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to be activated.

name: Magical Effect
summary: An effect is magical if it is created by a spell, a magic item, or a phenomenon that a rule labels as magical.

name: Malnutrition
summary: A creature needs an amount of food per day based on its size, as shown in the Food Needs per Day table.

name: Monster
summary: A monster is a creature controlled by the GM, even if the creature is benevolent.

name: Nonplayer Character
summary: A nonplayer character (NPC) is a monster that has a personal name and a distinct personality.

name: Object
summary: An object is a nonliving, distinct thing.

name: Occupied Space
summary: A space is occupied if a creature is in it or if it is completely filled by objects.

name: Opportunity Attacks
summary: You can make an Opportunity Attack when a creature that you can see leaves your reach using its action, its Bonus Action, its Reaction, or one of its speeds.

name: Paralyzed
summary: While you have the Paralyzed condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Passive Perception
summary: Passive Perception is a score that reflects a creature’s general awareness of its surroundings.

name: Per Day
summary: If a rule says you can use something a certain number of times per day, that means you must finish a Long Rest to use it again after you run out of uses.

name: Petrified
summary: While you have the Petrified condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Player Character
summary: A player character is a character controlled by a player.

name: Poisoned
summary: While you have the Poisoned condition, you experience the following effect.

name: Possession
summary: Some effects cause a creature to be possessed by another creature or entity.

name: Proficiency
summary: If you have proficiency with something, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to any D20 Test you make using that thing.

name: Prone
summary: While you have the Prone condition, you experience the following effects.

name: Reach
summary: A creature has a reach of 5 feet unless a rule says otherwise.

name: Reaction
summary: A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction’s description.

name: Ready

name: 1: Choose Abilities
summary: Choose three abilities that seem appropriate for the background:

name: 2: Choose a Feat
summary: Choose one feat from the Origin category.

name: 3: Choose Skill Proficiencies
summary: Choose two skills appropriate for the background.

summary: Choose one tool used in the practice of the background or often associated with it.

name: 5: Choose Equipment
summary: Assemble a package of equipment worth 50 GP (including unspent gold).

name: Abilities
summary: A sentient magic item has Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores.

name: Ability Checks
summary: An ability check represents a creature using talent and training to try to overcome a challenge, such as forcing open a stuck door, picking a lock, entertaining a crowd, or deciphering a cipher.

name: Ability Checks
summary: Ability checks can be key in determining the outcome of a social interaction.

name: Ability Modifier
summary: An ability check is named for the ability modifier it uses: a Strength check, an Intelligence check, and so on.

name: Ability Modifier
summary: The Attack Roll Abilities table shows which ability modifier to use for different types of attack rolls.

name: Ability Modifier
summary: Saving throws are named for the ability modifiers they use: a Constitution saving throw, a Wisdom saving throw, and so on.

name: Ability Modifiers
summary: Each ability has a modifier that you apply whenever you make a D20 Test with that ability (explained in “D20 Tests”).

name: Ability Scores
summary: A background lists three of your character’s ability scores.

name: Ability Scores
summary: Every monster has six ability scores along with corresponding ability score modifiers and saving throw modifiers.

name: Ability Scores
summary: Each ability has a score from 1 to 20, although some monsters have a score as high as 30.

name: Actions
summary: A monster can take the actions in this section or take one of the actions available to all creatures, as described in “Playing the Game.”

name: Actions
summary: When you do something other than moving or communicating, you typically take an action.

name: Activating a Magic Item
summary: It usually takes a Magic action to activate a magic item.

name: Adjust Ability Scores
summary: After assigning your ability scores, adjust them according to your background.

name: Adjustments
summary: A player’s absence might warrant removing creatures from an encounter to keep it at the intended difficulty.

name: Advantage/Disadvantage
summary: Sometimes a D20 Test is modified by Advantage or Disadvantage.

name: Adventuring Equipment
summary: As adventurers explore, their equipment can help them in many ways.

name: Adventuring Gear
summary: The Adventuring Gear table in this section includes gear that adventurers often find useful.

name: Alignment
summary: A sentient magic item has an alignment.

name: Alignment
summary: The alignment specified in a monster’s stat block is a default suggestion of how to roleplay the monster, inspired by its traditional role in the game or realworld folklore.

name: Always-Prepared Spells
summary: Certain features might give you a spell that you always have prepared.

name: Ammunition and Ranged Attacks
summary: A monster that requires ammunition to make ranged attacks carries the necessary ammunition.

name: Arcana Proficiency
summary: To craft a magic item, you and any assistants must have proficiency in the Arcana skill.

name: Armor
summary: The Armor table lists the game’s main armor.

name: Armor
summary: An item in the Armor category is typically a magical version of armor from “Equipment.” Unless an armor’s description notes otherwise, the armor must be worn for its magic to function.

name: Armor Class
summary: If you have multiple ways to calculate your Armor Class, you can benefit from only one at a time.

name: Armor Class
summary: A monster’s Armor Class (AC) includes its natural armor, Dexterity, gear, and other defenses.

name: Armor Class
summary: A creature’s Armor Class represents how well the creature avoids being wounded in combat.

name: Armor Training
summary: Anyone can don armor or hold a Shield, but only those with training can use them effectively, as explained below.

name: Artisan’s Tools
summary: Artisan’s Tools are each focused on crafting items and pursuing a trade.

name: Assassin’s Blood (150 GP)
summary: Ingested Poison

name: Assign Ability Scores
summary: Once you’ve generated six scores, assign them to Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma, keeping in mind your class’s primary ability.

name: Attack Notation
summary: The entry for a monster’s attack identifies whether the attack is a melee or a ranged attack and then provides the attack roll’s bonus, its reach or range, and what happens on a hit.

name: Attack Rolls
summary: An attack roll determines whether an attack hits a target.

name: Attack Rolls
summary: Some spells require the caster to make an attack roll to determine whether the spell hits a target.

name: Attune during a Short Rest
summary: Attuning to an item requires you to spend a Short Rest focused on only that item while being in physical contact with it (this can’t be the same Short Rest used to learn the item’s properties).

name: Attunement
summary: Some magic items require a creature to form a bond—called Attunement—with them before the creature can use an item’s magical properties.

name: Barding
summary: Barding is armor designed for a mount.

name: Bestow Curse
summary: The simplest curses are created by the Bestow Curse spell.

name: Bonus Action
summary: If a monster has Bonus Action options, they are listed in this section.

name: Bonus Actions
summary: Various class features, spells, and other abilities let you take an additional action on your turn called a Bonus Action.

name: Breaking Objects
summary: As an action, you can automatically break or otherwise destroy a fragile, nonmagical object, such as a glass container or a piece of paper.

name: Breaking Up Your Move
summary: You can break up your move, using some of its movement before and after any action, Bonus Action, or Reaction you take on the same turn.

name: Brewing Potions of Healing
summary: A character who has proficiency with the Herbalism Kit can create a Potion of Healing.

name: Burnt Othur Fumes (500 GP)
summary: Inhaled Poison

name: Cackle Fever
summary: Magical Contagion

name: Cantrips
summary: If the scribed spell is a cantrip, the version on the scroll works as if the caster were your level.

name: Carrying Objects
summary: You can usually carry your gear and treasure without worrying about the weight of those objects.

name: Casting Spells
summary: Each spell description has a series of entries that provide the details needed to cast the spell.

name: Casting Time
summary: Most spells require the Magic action to cast, but some spells require a Bonus Action, a Reaction, or 1 minute or more.

name: Casting without Slots
summary: There are several ways to cast a spell without expending a spell slot:

name: Challenge Rating
summary: Challenge Rating is defined in “Rules Glossary,” while guidance on using CR to plan potential combat encounters is in “Gameplay Toolbox.”

name: Character Backgrounds
summary: Your character’s background is a collection of characteristics that represent the place and occupation that were most formative before your character embarked on a life of adventure.

name: Character Demise
summary: If your character dies, others might find a magical way to revive your character, such as with the Raise Dead spell.

name: Character Species
summary: When you choose your character’s species, you determine whether your character is a human or a member of a fantastical species, such as dragonborn or gnome.

name: Charges
summary: Some magic items have charges that must be expended to activate their properties.

name: Choose a Background
summary: Choose your character’s background, and write it on your character sheet.

name: Choose a Character Sheet
summary: You’ll record the main details of your character on a character sheet.

name: Choose a Species
summary: Choose a species for your character.

name: Choose Languages
summary: Your character knows at least three languages: Common plus two languages you roll or choose from the Standard Languages table.

name: Choose Starting Equipment
summary: Your background and class both provide starting equipment.

name: Class Features
summary: When you gain a new level in a class, you get its features for that level.

name: Class Spell Lists
summary: If a spell is on a class’s spell list, the class’s name appears in parentheses after the spell’s school of magic.

name: Coins
summary: Characters often find coins on their adventures and can spend those coins in shops, inns, and other businesses.

name: Collapsing Roof
summary: Deadly Trap (Levels 1–4)

name: Combat
summary: Adventurers encounter many dangerous monsters and nefarious villains.

name: Combat Encounter Difficulty
summary: Use the following guidelines to create a combat encounter of a desired level of difficulty.

name: Combat Encounters
summary: The following features can make a combat encounter more interesting or challenging:

name: Combat Step by Step
summary: Combat unfolds in these steps:

name: Combining Spell Effects
summary: The effects of different spells add together while their durations overlap.

name: Command Word
summary: A command word is a word or short phrase that must be spoken or signed for an item to work.

name: Communication
summary: A sentient item communicates by sharing its emotions, broadcasting its thoughts telepathically, or speaking aloud.

name: Components
summary: A spell’s components are physical requirements the spellcaster must meet to cast the spell.

name: Conflict
summary: When the bearer of a sentient item acts in a manner opposed to the item’s alignment or purpose, conflict can arise.

name: Consumable Items
summary: Some items are consumed—used up, in other words—when they are activated.

name: Controlling a Mount
summary: You can control a mount only if it has been trained to accept a rider.

name: Cover
summary: Walls, trees, creatures, and other obstacles can provide cover, making a target more difficult to harm.

name: CR 0 Creatures
summary: Creatures that have a CR of 0, particularly ones that are worth 0 XP, should be used sparingly.

name: Crafting Magic Items
summary: “Equipment” contains rules on brewing Potions of Healing and scribing Spell Scrolls.

name: Crafting Nonmagical Items
summary: To craft a nonmagical item, you need tools, raw materials, and time, each of which is detailed below.

name: Create Your Character
summary: Here are the steps to make a character; each step is explored in detail:

name: Creating a Background
summary: A character’s background represents what the character did prior to becoming an adventurer.

name: Creating Your Character
summary: Creating a higher-level character uses the same character-creation steps outlined in this chapter and the rules for advancing beyond level 1 provided in the “Level Advancement” section.

name: Creature Size
summary: A creature belongs to a size category, which determines the width of the square space the creature occupies on a map, as shown on the Creature Size and Space table.

name: Creature Type
summary: A character’s species determines the character’s creature type, which is described in “Rules Glossary.” Every species in “Character Origins” is Humanoid; playable non-Humanoid species appear in other books.

name: Creature Type
summary: Each monster has a tag that identifies the type of creature it is.

name: Crew
summary: A ship larger than a Keelboat or Rowboat needs a crew of skilled hirelings (see “Hirelings” later in “Equipment”) to function.

name: Critical Hits
summary: When you score a Critical Hit, you deal extra damage.

name: Cursed Creatures
summary: Some monsters are associated with curses, whether as part of their origins or due to their ability to spread curses—werewolves being a prime example.

name: Cursed Items
summary: A magic item’s description specifies whether it bears a curse.

name: Cursed Magic Items
summary: Cursed magic items are created deliberately or originate as the result of supernatural events.

name: Curses
summary: A curse typically takes one of the forms detailed below.

name: Curses and Magical Contagions
summary: A curse is a magical burden that lasts for a specified time or until it is ended by some means.

name: D20 Tests
summary: When the outcome of an action is uncertain, the game uses a d20 roll to determine success or failure.

name: Damage against Multiple Targets
summary: When you create a damaging effect that forces two or more targets to make saving throws against it at the same time, roll the damage once for all the targets.

name: Damage and Healing
summary: Injury and death are frequent threats, as detailed in the following rules.

name: Damage Notation
summary: A stat block usually provides both a number and a die expression for each instance of damage.

name: Damage Rolls
summary: Each weapon, spell, and damaging monster ability specifies the damage it deals.

name: Damage Threshold
summary: If a vehicle has a damage threshold (see “Rules Glossary”), it’s noted in the table.

name: Damage Types
summary: Each instance of damage has a type, like Fire or Slashing.

name: Death Saving Throws
summary: Whenever you start your turn with 0 Hit Points, you must make a Death Saving Throw to determine whether you creep closer to death or hang on to life.

name: Deep Water
summary: Swimming through deep water (more than 100 feet deep) presents additional challenges because of the water’s pressure and cold temperature.

name: Descriptive Tags
summary: A monster might have one or more tags in parentheses following its type.

name: Determine Ability Modifiers
summary: Finally, determine your ability modifiers using the Ability Scores and Modifiers table.

name: Determining Skills
summary: A character’s starting skill proficiencies are determined at character creation, and a monster’s skill proficiencies appear in its stat block.

name: Difficult Terrain
summary: Combatants are often slowed down by Difficult Terrain.

name: Difficulty Class
summary: The Difficulty Class of an ability check represents the task’s difficulty.

name: Difficulty Class
summary: The Difficulty Class for a saving throw is determined by the effect that causes it or by the GM.

name: Dropping Prone
summary: On your turn, you can give yourself the Prone condition (see “Rules Glossary”) without using an action or any of your Speed, but you can’t do so if your Speed is 0.

name: Dropping to 0 Hit Points
summary: When a creature drops to 0 Hit Points, it either dies outright or falls unconscious, as explained below.

name: Duration
summary: Temporary Hit Points last until they’re depleted or you finish a Long Rest (see “Rules Glossary”).

name: Duration
summary: A spell’s duration is the length of time the spell persists after it is cast.

name: Effects
summary: The effects of a spell are detailed after its duration entry.

name: Ending Attunement
summary: Your Attunement to an item ends if you no longer satisfy the prerequisites for Attunement, if the item has been more than 100 feet away for at least 24 hours, if you die, or if another creature attunes to the item.

name: Ending Combat
summary: Combat ends when one side or the other is defeated, which can mean the creatures are killed or knocked out or have surrendered or fled.

name: Environmental Curses
summary: Some locations are so suffused with evil that anyone who lingers there is burdened with a curse.

name: Equipment
summary: Each background offers a choice between a package of equipment and 50 GP.

name: Equipment Proficiencies
summary: A character gains proficiency with various weapons and tools from their class and background.

name: Equipping a Monster with Other Items
summary: You may equip monsters with additional gear however you like, using the items in “Equipment” for inspiration.

summary: Inhaled Poison

name: Example Contagions
summary: The following examples show how magical contagions can work.

name: Example Traps
summary: Traps are presented in alphabetical order.

name: Experience Points
summary: The Experience Point cost to gain a level is based on your total character level, not your level in a particular class, as shown in the Character Advancement table in “Character Creation.” For example, if you are a level 6 Cleric / level 1 Fighter, you must gain enough XP to reach level 8 before…

name: Experience Points
summary: The number of Experience Points (XP) a monster is worth is based on its CR, as detailed in the Experience Points by Challenge Rating table.

name: Exploration
summary: Exploration involves delving into places that are dangerous and full of mystery.

name: Extended Travel
summary: Characters can push themselves to travel for more than 8 hours per day, at the risk of tiring.

name: Extra Attack
summary: If you gain the Extra Attack feature from more than one class, the features don’t stack.

name: Extreme Cold
summary: When the temperature is 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower, a creature exposed to the extreme cold must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour or gain 1 Exhaustion level.

name: Extreme Heat
summary: When the temperature is 100 degrees Fahrenheit or higher, a creature exposed to the extreme heat and without access to drinkable water must succeed on a Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour or gain 1 Exhaustion level.

name: Falling Net
summary: Nuisance Trap (Levels 1–4)

name: Falling Off
summary: If an effect is about to move your mount against its will while you’re on it, you must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall off, landing with the Prone condition (see “Rules Glossary”) in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the mount.

name: Falling Unconscious
summary: If you reach 0 Hit Points and don’t die instantly, you have the Unconscious condition (see “Rules Glossary”) until you regain any Hit Points, and you now face making Death Saving Throws (see below).

name: Fear and Mental Stress
summary: Due to the nature of their vocation, adventurers tend to be less susceptible to fear and mental stress than common folk.

name: Fear Effects
summary: Whenever the characters encounter something that is supernaturally frightful, use the Frightened condition as the baseline effect.

name: Feat
summary: A background gives your character a specified Origin feat (described in “Feats”).

name: Feat Descriptions
summary: The feats that follow are organized by category—Origin, General, Fighting Style, or Epic Boon—and alphabetized in each category.

name: Fill In Numbers
summary: Note these numbers on your character sheet.

name: Finding Hidden Objects
summary: When your character searches for hidden things, such as a secret door or a trap, the GM typically asks you to make a Wisdom (Perception) check, provided you describe the character searching in the hidden object’s vicinity.

name: Fire Resistance
summary: Anything underwater has Resistance to Fire damage (explained in “Damage and Healing”).

name: Fire-Casting Statue
summary: Deadly Trap (Levels 1–4)

name: Food, Drink, and Lodging
summary: The Food, Drink, and Lodging table gives prices for food and a single night’s lodging.

name: Frigid Water
summary: A creature can be immersed in frigid water for a number of minutes equal to its Constitution score before suffering any ill effects.

name: Gaining a Level
summary: When you gain a level, follow these steps:

name: Gaining Spells
summary: Before you can cast a spell, you must have the spell prepared in your mind or have access to the spell from a magic item, such as a Spell Scroll.

name: Gear
summary: Monsters have proficiency with their equipment.

name: Generate Your Scores
summary: Determine your ability scores by using one of the following three methods.

name: Glossary Conventions
summary: The glossary uses the following conventions:

name: Good Roads
summary: The presence of a good road increases the group’s maximum pace by one step (from Slow to Normal or from Normal to Fast).

name: Half Damage
summary: Many saving throw effects deal half damage (round down) to a target when the target succeeds on the saving throw.

name: Harvesting Poison
summary: A character can attempt to harvest poison from a venomous creature that is dead or has the Incapacitated condition.

name: Hazards
summary: Monsters are the main perils characters face, but other dangers await.

name: Healing
summary: Hit Points can be restored by magic, such as the Cure Wounds spell or a Potion of Healing, or by a Short or Long Rest (see “Rules Glossary”).

name: Heavy Precipitation
summary: Everything within an area of heavy rain or heavy snowfall is Lightly Obscured, and creatures in the area have Disadvantage on all Wisdom (Perception) checks.

name: Hidden Pit
summary: Nuisance Trap (Levels 1–4)

name: Hiding
summary: Adventurers and monsters often hide, whether to spy on one another, sneak past a guardian, or set an ambush.

name: High Altitude
summary: Traveling at altitudes of 10,000 feet or higher above sea level is taxing for most creatures because of the reduced amount of oxygen in the air.

name: Hirelings
summary: Skilled hirelings include anyone hired to perform a service that involves a proficiency (including weapon, tool, or skill): a mercenary, an artisan, a scribe, or the like.

name: Hit Points
summary: A monster’s Hit Points are presented as a number followed by parentheses, where the monster’s Hit Point Dice are provided, along with any contribution from its Constitution.

name: Hit Points
summary: Hit Points represent durability and the will to live.

name: Hit Points and Hit Point Dice
summary: You gain the Hit Points from your new class as described for levels after 1.

name: Identifying a Magic Item
summary: Some magic items are indistinguishable from their nonmagical counterparts, while others are conspicuously magical.

name: Imagine Your Past and Present
summary: Let your character’s background and species inspire how you imagine their past.

name: Immunities
summary: This entry lists the monster’s Immunities, if any.

name: Immunity
summary: Some creatures and objects have Immunity to certain damage types and conditions.

name: Impeded Weapons
summary: When making a melee attack roll with a weapon underwater, a creature that lacks a Swim Speed has Disadvantage on the attack roll unless the weapon deals Piercing damage.

name: Initiative
summary: The Initiative entry specifies the monster’s Initiative modifier followed by the monster’s Initiative score in parentheses.

name: Initiative
summary: Initiative determines the order of turns during combat.

name: Instant Death
summary: Here are the main ways a creature can die instantly.

name: Interacting with Objects
summary: Interacting with objects is often simple to resolve.

name: Interactions with Rerolls
summary: When you have Advantage or Disadvantage and something in the game lets you reroll or replace the d20, you can reroll or replace only one die, not both.

name: Languages
summary: This entry lists languages that the monster can use to communicate.

name: Large Vehicles
summary: The Airborne and Waterborne Vehicles table provides statistics for various types of large vehicles.

name: Legendary Actions
summary: If the monster has Legendary Action options, those are listed in this section.

name: Level Advancement
summary: While going on adventures, your character gains experience, represented by Experience Points (XP).

name: Lifestyle Expenses
summary: Lifestyle expenses summarize the cost of living in a fantasy world.

name: Light
summary: The presence or absence of light determines the category of illumination in an area, as defined below.

name: Light, Medium, or Heavy Armor
summary: If you wear Light, Medium, or Heavy armor and lack training with it, you have Disadvantage on any D20 Test that involves Strength or Dexterity, and you can’t cast spells.

name: Limited Usage
summary: Some parts of a stat block have restrictions on the number of times they can be used.

name: Longer Casting Times
summary: Certain spells—including a spell cast as a Ritual—require more time to cast: minutes or even hours.

name: Lose Temporary Hit Points First
summary: If you have Temporary Hit Points and take damage, those points are lost first, and any leftover damage carries over to your Hit Points.

name: Magic Item Categories
summary: Every magic item belongs to a category.

name: Magic Item Rarity
summary: Every magic item has a rarity, which provides a rough measure of an item’s power relative to other magic items.

name: Magic Item Resilience
summary: A magic item is at least as durable as a nonmagical item of its kind.

name: Magic Item Values by Rarity
summary: Common magic items can often be bought in a town or city.

name: Magic Items
summary: Adventures hold the promise—but not a guarantee—of finding magic items.

name: Magic Items
summary: Magic items are gleaned from the hoards of felled monsters or discovered in long-lost vaults.

name: Magic Items A–Z
summary: Magic items are presented in alphabetical order.

name: Magical Contagions
summary: Alchemists, potion brewers, and areas of wild magic are credited with creating the first magical contagions.

name: Making an Attack
summary: When you take the Attack action, you make an attack.

name: Malice (250 GP)
summary: Inhaled Poison

name: Many Creatures
summary: The more creatures in an encounter, the higher the risk that a lucky streak on their part could deal more damage to the characters than you expect.

name: Mastery Properties
summary: Each weapon has a mastery property, which is usable only by a character who has a feature, such as Weapon Mastery, that unlocks the property for the character.

name: Material (M)
summary: A Material component is a particular material used in a spell’s casting, as specified in parentheses in the Components entry.

name: Melee Attacks
summary: A melee attack allows you to attack a target within your reach.

name: Mental Stress Effects
summary: When a character is subjected to an effect that causes intense mental stress, Psychic damage is the best way to emulate that effect.

name: Midnight Tears (1,500 GP)
summary: Ingested Poison

name: Mounted Combat
summary: A willing creature that is at least one size larger than a rider and that has an appropriate anatomy can serve as a mount, using the following rules.

name: Mounting and Dismounting
summary: During your move, you can mount a creature that is within 5 feet of you or dismount.

name: Mounts and Cargo
summary: An animal pulling a carriage, cart, chariot, sled, or wagon can move weight up to five times its base carrying capacity, including the weight of the vehicle.

name: Mounts and Vehicles

name: Opportunity Attacks

name: Proficiency

name: Proficiency Bonus

name: Proficiency Bonus

name: Proficiency Bonus

name: Proficiency Bonus

name: Prolonged Effects

name: Range

name: Range

name: Ranged Attacks
summary: When you make a ranged attack, you fire a bow, hurl an axe, or otherwise send projectiles to strike a foe at a distance.

name: Ranged Attacks in Close Combat
summary: Aiming a ranged attack is more difficult when a foe is next to you.

name: Raw Materials
summary: To make an item, you need raw materials worth half its purchase cost (round down).

name: Reach

name: Reaction and Bonus Action Triggers
summary: A spell that has a casting time of a Reaction is cast in response to a trigger that is defined in the spell’s Casting Time entry.

name: Reactions

name: Reactions

name: Record Class Features

name: Resistance and Vulnerability
summary: Some creatures and objects have Resistance or Vulnerability to certain damage types.

summary: These entries list a monster’s Resistances and Vulnerabilities, if any.

name: Rest and Recuperation
summary: If a creature infected with a magical contagion spends 3 days recuperating—engaging in no activities that would interrupt a Long Rest—the creature makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw at the end of the recuperation period.

name: Rhythm of Play
summary: The three main pillars of D&D play are social interaction, exploration, and combat.

name: Rings
summary: For its magic to function, an item in the Ring category must be worn on a finger or a similar digit unless its description notes otherwise.

name: Rods
summary: An item in the Rod category is a scepter usually made of metal, wood, or bone.

name: Roleplaying
summary: Roleplaying is, literally, the act of playing out a role.

name: Roll Two D20s

name: Rolling 20 or 1

name: Saving Throw Proficiencies
summary: Proficiency in a saving throw lets a character add their Proficiency Bonus to saves that use a particular ability.

name: Saving Throws
summary: A saving throw—also called a save—represents an attempt to evade or resist a threat, such as a fiery explosion, a blast of poisonous gas, or a spell trying to invade your mind.

name: Saving Throws

name: Saving Throws and Damage
summary: Damage dealt via saving throws uses these rules.

name: School of Magic

name: Scrolls

name: Senses

name: Senses

name: Size

name: Skill Proficiencies

name: Skill Proficiencies
summary: Most ability checks involve using a skill, which represents a category of things creatures try to do with an ability check.

name: Skills
summary: The Skills entry specifies a monster’s skill proficiencies, if any.

name: Social Interaction

name: Somatic (S)
summary: A Somatic component is a forceful gesticulation or an intricate set of gestures.

name: Special Purpose

name: Special Senses
summary: Some creatures have special senses that help them perceive things in certain situations.

name: Special Traits
summary: Each species gives a character special traits—unique characteristics based on the species’ physiology or magical nature.

name: Speed

name: Speed
summary: The Speed entry specifies a monster’s Speed.

name: Spell Level

name: Spell Slots
summary: Spellcasting is taxing, so a spellcaster can cast only a limited number of level 1+ spells before resting.

name: Spellcasting
summary: Your capacity for spellcasting depends partly on your combined levels in all your spellcasting classes and partly on your individual levels in those classes.

name: Spellcasting

name: The Nine Alignments

summary: Temporary Hit Points can’t be added to your Hit Points, healing can’t restore them, and receiving Temporary Hit Points doesn’t count as healing.

name: Tier 2 (Levels 5–10)

name: Tier 3 (Levels 11–16)

name: Tier 4 (Levels 17–20)

summary: You imbue plants in an immobile 30-foot Emanation with limited sentience and animation, giving them the ability to communicate with you and follow your simple commands.

name: Spider Climb
summary: Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch gains the ability to move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and along ceilings, while leaving its hands free.

name: Spike Growth
summary: The ground in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range sprouts hard spikes and thorns.

name: Spirit Guardians
summary: Protective spirits flit around you in a 15-foot Emanation for the duration.

name: Spiritual Weapon
summary: You create a floating, spectral force that resembles a weapon of your choice and lasts for the duration.

name: Starry Wisp
summary: You launch a mote of light at one creature or object within range.

name: Stinking Cloud
summary: You create a 20-foot-radius Sphere of yellow, nauseating gas centered on a point within range.

name: Stone Shape
summary: You touch a stone object of Medium size or smaller or a section of stone no more than 5 feet in any dimension and form it into any shape you like.

name: Stoneskin
summary: Until the spell ends, one willing creature you touch has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

name: Storm of Vengeance
summary: A churning storm cloud forms for the duration, centered on a point within range and spreading to a radius of 300 feet.

name: Suggestion
summary: You suggest a course of activity—described in no more than 25 words—to one creature you can see within range that can hear and understand you.

name: Summon Dragon
summary: You call forth a Dragon spirit.

name: Sunbeam
summary: You launch a sunbeam in a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long Line.

name: Sunburst
summary: Brilliant sunlight flashes in a 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within range.

name: Symbol
summary: You inscribe a harmful glyph either on a surface (such as a section of floor or wall) or within an object that can be closed (such as a book or chest).

name: Telekinesis
summary: You gain the ability to move or manipulate creatures or objects by thought.

name: Telepathic Bond
summary: You forge a telepathic link among up to eight willing creatures of your choice within range, psychically linking each creature to all the others for the duration.

name: Teleport
summary: This spell instantly transports you and up to eight willing creatures that you can see within range, or a single object that you can see within range, to a destination you select.

name: Teleportation Circle
summary: As you cast the spell, you draw a 5-foot-radius circle on the ground inscribed with sigils that link your location to a permanent teleportation circle of your choice whose sigil sequence you know and that is on the same plane of existence as you.

name: Thaumaturgy
summary: You manifest a minor wonder within range.

name: Thunderwave
summary: You unleash a wave of thunderous energy.

name: Time Stop
summary: You briefly stop the flow of time for everyone but yourself.

name: Tiny Hut
summary: A 10-foot Emanation springs into existence around you and remains stationary for the duration.

name: Tongues
summary: This spell grants the creature you touch the ability to understand any spoken or signed language that it hears or sees.

name: Transport via Plants
summary: This spell creates a magical link between a Large or larger inanimate plant within range and another plant, at any distance, on the same plane of existence.

name: Tree Stride
summary: You gain the ability to enter a tree and move from inside it to inside another tree of the same kind within 500 feet.

name: True Polymorph
summary: Choose one creature or nonmagical object that you can see within range.

name: True Resurrection
summary: You touch a creature that has been dead for no longer than 200 years and that died for any reason except old age.

name: True Seeing
summary: For the duration, the willing creature you touch has Truesight with a range of 120 feet.

name: True Strike
summary: Guided by a flash of magical insight, you make one attack with the weapon used in the spell’s casting.

name: Tsunami
summary: A wall of water springs into existence at a point you choose within range.

name: Unseen Servant
summary: This spell creates an Invisible, mindless, shapeless, Medium force that performs simple tasks at your command until the spell ends.

name: Vampiric Touch
summary: The touch of your shadow-wreathed hand can siphon life force from others to heal your wounds.

name: Vicious Mockery
summary: You unleash a string of insults laced with subtle enchantments at one creature you can see or hear within range.

name: Vitriolic Sphere
summary: You point at a location within range, and a glowing, 1-foot-diameter ball of acid streaks there and explodes in a 20-foot-radius Sphere.

name: Wall of Fire
summary: You create a wall of fire on a solid surface within range.

name: Wall of Force
summary: An Invisible wall of force springs into existence at a point you choose within range.

name: Wall of Ice
summary: You create a wall of ice on a solid surface within range.

name: Wall of Stone
summary: A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into existence at a point you choose within range.

name: Wall of Thorns
summary: You create a wall of tangled brush bristling with needle-sharp thorns.

name: Warding Bond
summary: You touch another creature that is willing and create a mystic connection between you and the target until the spell ends.

name: Water Breathing
summary: This spell grants up to ten willing creatures of your choice within range the ability to breathe underwater until the spell ends.

name: Water Walk
summary: This spell grants the ability to move across any liquid surface—such as water, acid, mud, snow, quicksand, or lava—as if it were harmless solid ground (creatures crossing molten lava can still take damage from the heat).

name: Web
summary: You conjure a mass of sticky webbing at a point within range.

name: Weird
summary: You try to create illusory terrors in others’ minds.

name: Wind Walk
summary: You and up to ten willing creatures of your choice within range assume gaseous forms for the duration, appearing as wisps of cloud.

name: Wind Wall
summary: A wall of strong wind rises from the ground at a point you choose within range.

name: Wish
summary: Wish is the mightiest spell a mortal can cast.

name: Word of Recall
summary: You and up to five willing creatures within 5 feet of you instantly teleport to a previously designated sanctuary.

name: Zone of Truth
summary: You create a magical zone that guards against deception in a 15-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point within range.

name: Ammunition
summary: You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it.

name: Finesse
summary: When making an attack with a Finesse weapon, use your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

name: Heavy
summary: You have Disadvantage on attack rolls with a Heavy weapon if it’s a Melee weapon and your Strength score isn’t at least 13 or if it’s a Ranged weapon and your Dexterity score isn’t at least 13.

name: Light
summary: When you take the Attack action on your turn and attack with a Light weapon, you can make one extra attack as a Bonus Action later on the same turn.

name: Loading
summary: You can fire only one piece of ammunition from a Loading weapon when you use an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction to fire it, regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

name: Range
summary: A Range weapon has a range in parentheses after the Ammunition or Thrown property.

name: Reach
summary: A Reach weapon adds 5 feet to your reach when you attack with it, as well as when determining your reach for Opportunity Attacks with it.

name: Thrown
summary: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack.

name: Two-Handed
summary: A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.

name: Versatile
summary: A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands.
